newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST--Fiat set for H1 1996 profit dip.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST--Fiat set for H1 1996 profit dip.

text.p: Italian automotive and industrial group Fiat is set to see a fall in first-year 1996 profits due to hefty start-up costs of new vehicles, a depressed Italian car market and the effect of the higher lira, analysts said.

They expect the Turin-based group to report on September 19 first half 1996 pretax profits between 1.1 trillion and 1.6 trillion lire ($720 million-$1 billion) after a 1995 first half pretax profit of 2.153 trillion lire.

Analysts will be looking for any words of encouragement on the Italian car market, progress in its important Brazilian market and any further pointers towards the flotation of its New Holland tractors and agricultural machinery business.

Nick Potter, analyst at Credito Italiano, said the group's first half operating margin could be as low as three percent after 5.2 percent in the first half of 1995 while group turnover is expected to grow seven percent to 41.5 trillion lire.

He pointed to the start-up costs for new models in New Holland, Iveco and Fiat Auto and the sluggish performance of the Italian car market, with no recovery yet in sight, as depressing the group's first half profits.
Bob Barber, analyst at brokers James Capel, who is forecasting a first-half pretax figure of 1.6 trillion lire said he will be looking for an update on Fiat's position in Brazil.

In the first quarter of 1996, Fiat absorbed heavy start up costs for its new world car the Palio, while production was not yet up to speed in the second quarter, but is now hitting target production of 2,000 cars a day.

Barber pointed out that last year's first half pre-tax figure of 2.153 trillion lire included 380 billion lire of extraordinary gains. When stripping out these gains, the fall in first pre-tax 1996 numbers will not be as dramatic.
